newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala 1996 inflation rate 10.85 pct - gov't.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala 1996 inflation rate 10.85 pct - gov't.

text.p: Guatemalan consumer prices rose 10.85 percent in 1996, compared to 8.61 percent in 1995, the National Statistic Institute said on Wednesday.
The Bank of Guatemala had predicted inflation rates of eight to ten percent for 1996.
"We feel that while inflation was a little bit over the goals, it was within a reasonably controllable level," Economy Minister Juan Mauricio Wurmser told a news conference.
Wurmser said average inflation for Guatemala has been 11 percent over the last five years, so 1996 inflation was not outside the normal range.
The minister said Guatemala's inflation rate for 1996 was lower than most of the rest of Central America.
Guatemalan consumer prices rose 0.87 percent in December, compared to a rise of 0.49 percent in the same month of 1995, according to the National Statistic Institute said.
